core_connection.text: Audible's customer service team, which Mia contacts to cancel her Audible Premium Plus membership and get refunds for charges she did not use.

evidence.quote: cancel my Audible Premium Plus membership
cancel the membership and refund the $14.95 charge
request a refund for the months I did not use
please go ahead with the refund

facts.text: This is Audible's customer service desk. Mia writes to it as a subscriber about billing, cancelling and refunds.
Mia had an Audible Premium Plus membership that cost $14.95 a month.
In March 2025, Mia asked to cancel and get a refund for five unused months (November 2024 to March 2025), $74.75 in total. She had not listened to anything since October 2024.

evidence.quote: not downloaded or listened to any title

facts.text: Audible refunded only the March 2025 charge of $14.95. Mia then asked for the other four charges, $59.80 for November 2024 to February 2025, to be refunded as well.
Mia wants refunds paid back to her original payment method, not kept as account credits, and she asked for the unused credits to be removed.

evidence.quote: The credits can be removed from my account.

facts.text: In March 2025, Mia said she did not plan to use the service again.

evidence.quote: plan to use the service again

facts.text: On November 8, 2025, Mia paused her membership and set it to cancel when the pause ended on February 8, 2026.

evidence.quote: end of the pause on February 8, 2026

facts.text: The membership renewed anyway on February 8, 2026, and Mia was charged $14.95. She asked Audible to cancel it, refund the charge and confirm there would be no more charges.

evidence.quote: no further charges will be made

facts.text: On February 12, 2026, Mia confirmed that Audible should go ahead with the $14.95 refund.

evidence.quote: please go ahead with the refund

facts.text: Mia's emails to Audible are short and polite. They state exact amounts and dates and end by asking Audible to confirm the cancellation and the refund.
